item.title: Why are we doing this?
item.description:
Why are we doing this? #

One page, before any terminal.

You can now build real software by describing it — what people call vibe coding: you say what you want, a model writes it, you steer. It works, startlingly well. And it has a failure mode everyone who tries it eventually hits: three weeks in, neither you nor the model remembers why anything is the way it is. The code is there; the reasoning evaporated with the chat window it happened in.

item.title: Chapter 2 — Setting up your tools
item.description:
Chapter 2 — Setting up your tools #

macOS path. Windows readers: tentative notes are marked — we haven’t walked them end-to-end yet, and we’d genuinely value your corrections ( open an issue with the step ID). Budget 30–45 minutes, mostly waiting on installers. This chapter opens by installing the helper — so every later step has someone to ask.

Each tool comes with its why — “install these five things” with no reasons is the style this methodology replaces.

item.title: Chapter 3 — Your first project
item.description:
Chapter 3 — Your first project #

A real project: a Wordle variant, live on GitHub Pages, built with a model collaborator — and your first decisions on the record. Budget ~60 minutes; each step shows its own estimate, and your actual times are something we genuinely want to hear about. One path; each step says how to verify it worked.

A GitHub account ~4 min

☰
GitHub is where your project’s code, its decision records, and (in a few steps) its live website all live. If you already have an account, enter your username below and skip to P2.

Go to github.com/signup. Don’t stall on the username — you can change it later (Settings → Account), add or swap email addresses, all of it. Pick something and move.

item.title: Tell us what happened
item.description:
Tell us what happened #

Two minutes, two moves — and if you’re reading this page because you’re stopping partway, that’s exactly as valuable: tell us where and why (ten seconds, three boxes), and thank you — the walkers who stop are the ones a guide learns the most from.

The debrief — a record, like everything else ~5 min

☰

Builds on: Your first answers, four ways

item.title: Your variables
item.description:
Your variables #

This guide personalizes itself. Two values, entered once, appear in every command that needs them — so what you copy-paste is already yours, not a template you have to patch by hand.

Where they live: in your browser’s local storage, and nowhere else. They never leave your machine, we never see them, and clearing your browser data clears them (the guide then just shows the placeholders again). You can change them here any time and every page updates.
